text:
maria: FYI customer on GCP just hit a hard 401s after they bumped from redwood-python 1.7.2 -> 1.9.0. They pinned the package so they couldn't roll back automatically.

alex: ugh. do we know if it's an auth header rename or a token format change? any repro?

maria: they supplied logs. error is `Invalid auth header` coming from our gateway. Curious thing: when they downgraded locally to 1.7.2 the same request works.

tim: can you paste the request/headers (sanitized) and the SDK call?

maria: pasted below (sanitized):

```
# client code
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['RW_KEY'])
resp = client.generate("Hello")
```

Request headers captured by their proxy: `X-Auth: Bearer abc...` (instead of `Authorization: Bearer ...`)

maria: looks like 1.9.0 introduced a change in header name when using env var initialization under some packaging scenarios.

alex: oh that's the param renaming we thought we'd deprecated. sdk 1.9.0 has `auth_header_name` internal switch for cloud-init that defaulted to `X-Auth` for a specific constructor path. That should never be the default for normal clients.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-079 (support). Assigned to eng-sdk.

maria: customer also reported increased retries and doubled requests -> bill spike. They had `retry_total=3` in config expecting exponential backoff, but 1.9.0 changed default retry backoff to immediate retries in some code path.

oncall-ml: pinging @alex @nicholas from SDK team. Looks like two separate regressions: header default + retry backoff policy when client constructed from env.

alex: confirmed locally. Repro steps:
1) pip install redwood==1.9.0
2) export RW_INIT_MODE=auto (this triggers the env constructor path)
3) run the minimal snippet above\nObserved: outgoing header `X-Auth: Bearer <token>` and fast retries 0.1s between attempts.

nicholas: that env-specific path was added to support mesh-auth last quarter; we missed a config default override. I can draft a patch to restore `Authorization` and fix the backoff.

maria: customer is asking for mitigation now. They want either a pin recommendation or a config workaround.

tim: short mitigation: set RW_INIT_MODE=manual and construct client explicitly: `RedwoodClient(api_key=..., auth_header_name='Authorization', retry_backoff=0.5)` or pin to 1.7.2/1.8.3.

alex: agree. Also create a small snippet we can send to customer to avoid a redeploy: set env `RW_AUTH_HEADER=Authorization` (our legacy override still works).

maria: sent this to the customer:
- set RW_AUTH_HEADER=Authorization
- set RW_RETRY_STRATEGY=exponential
- or pip install redwood==1.8.3 to avoid 1.9.x

customer: (via email forwarded) can confirm setting RW_AUTH_HEADER fixed the 401s immediately. Still waiting to confirm billing impact.

oncall-ml: action items:
- @nicholas prepare 1.9.1 hotfix rolling back header default + restore exponential backoff (ETA 2h)
- @alex add integration test for env-init path to CI
- support to send pin/workaround to customer (maria)
- run a quick audit for other env vars introduced last quarter that may change defaults

nicholas: starting hotfix branch now, will push PR in ~45m.

alex: added unit test, raising PR for CI change.

support-bot: PR created: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4112

maria: thanks team. customer very happy about quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

tim: follow-up: can we add a small release note blurb so customers pinning will see the breaking change?

alex: yes. I'll add changelog entry and a deprecation notice in 1.9.1 release notes.

maria: closing loop when 1.9.1 released.

nicholas: PR merged and hotfix rolling to prod canary. patch version 1.9.1 will be cut after CI passes.

oncall-ml: can we also add a short FAQ in support KB about pinning and env-inits? customers keep pinning minor versions and we should warn about env-driven defaults.

maria: good idea, I'll draft the KB.

support-bot: Incident INC-2026-079 status: monitoring.

maria: closing thread here, will re-open if customer sees residual billing issues. :eyes:
